record.title: The logarithmic psd-rank conjecture for regular polygon slack matrices
record.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the slack matrix of the regular $n$-gon, and let $\operatorname{rank}_{\operatorname{psd}}(S_n)$ denote its positive semidefinite rank. **Logarithmic psd-rank conjecture.** The psd-rank of $S_n$ is given by

$$
\operatorname{rank}_{\operatorname{psd}}(S_n)=1+\lceil\log_2(n)\rceil.
$$

This conjecture proposes an exact logarithmic formula for the positive semidefinite rank of regular polygon slack matrices. The preceding computations support the formula for the smallest regular polygons and suggest it for $n\geq 7$, but the statement is not established in the provided text.
record.source_name: Arnaud Vandaele, François Glineur and Nicolas Gillis, “Algorithms for Positive Semidefinite Factorization”, arXiv:1707.07953 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.07953

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

record.title: Fabrici et al.'s four-color conjecture for facial unique-maximum edge-coloring
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a plane graph. Two distinct edges are **facially adjacent** if they are consecutive in some facial path, and a **facial edge-coloring** assigns distinct colors to facially adjacent edges. A **FUM-edge-coloring** is a facial edge-coloring in which each face is incident with a unique edge colored with the maximal color on that face. Write $\chi_{\mathrm{fum}}'(G)$ for the minimum number of colors in such a coloring.

**Fabrici et al.'s conjecture.** If $G$ is a $2$-edge-connected plane graph, then

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{fum}}'(G) \leq 4.
$$

The conjecture concerns the edge analogue of facial unique-maximum vertex-coloring. The paper proves the bound for $2$-connected plane graphs, but does not resolve the stated $2$-edge-connected version in full.
record.source_name: Vesna Andova, Bernard Lidický, Borut Lužar and Riste Škrekovski, “On facial unique-maximum (edge-)coloring”, arXiv:1708.00094 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.00094

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

record.title: The extremal representation conjecture for graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$, and let a **representation** of $G$ mean a graph representation in the sense of the paper. The **extremal representation conjecture.** The number of representations of a graph of order $n$ is maximized by the balanced complete bipartite graph of order $n$. This asks for the maximum possible number of representations among connected graphs of fixed order and identifies the balanced complete bipartite graph as an extremal graph; the conjecture is posed as an open problem for future research.
record.source_name: Péter G. N. Szabó, “A Characterization of Uniquely Representable Graphs”, arXiv:1708.01272 (2020).

record.title: Upper domination conjecture for direct products of complete multipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $K[a_i,b_i]$ denote the complete $b_i$-partite graph with $a_i$ vertices in each part, and let $G$ be its direct product

$$
G=
\prod_{i=1}^t K[a_i,b_i].
$$

Assume $2\leq b_1\leq b_2\leq\cdots\leq b_t$. The **upper domination conjecture.**

$$
\Gamma(G)=\frac{1}{b_1}\prod_{i=1}^t a_i b_i.
$$

Here $\Gamma(G)$ is the maximum size of a minimal dominating set of $G$. The proposition preceding the conjecture proves the corresponding lower bound, and the equality is known when $t\leq 3$ but remains open in general. A particularly attractive unresolved special case is $G=\prod_{i=1}^t K_3$.
record.source_name: Colin Defant and Sumun Iyer, “Domination and Upper Domination of Direct Product Graphs”, arXiv:1708.01305 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.01305

record.title: The conjecture for alpha in the intermediate partite range
record.statement:
Let $\alpha(k,r)$ be the parameter defined as the minimum number of edges between a specified independent transversal and its complement over all $K_r$-partite-saturated $k$-partite graphs, with $k\ge r\ge 3$. **The conjecture for $\alpha(k,r)$.** For

$$
5\le r\le k\le 2r-4,
$$

one has

$$
\alpha(k,r)=(k-1)(4r-k-6).
$$

The authors present this as the expected correct value of the upper bound in this range; the supplied text does not establish it.
record.source_name: António Girão, Teeradej Kittipassorn and Kamil Popielarz, “Partite Saturation of Complete Graphs”, arXiv:1708.01607 (2017).

record.title: Bukh's odd-reciprocal conjecture for equiangular lines
record.statement:
Let $N_\alpha(n)$ denote the maximum number of equiangular lines in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with common angle $\arccos\alpha$. **Bukh's conjecture.** If $1/\alpha$ is an odd natural number, then

$$
N_\alpha(n)=\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}\,n+O(1).
$$

The paper states that this is the first part of an earlier conjecture and that it was also raised by Bukh. The result proved in the paper covers the relevant range through the spectral-radius-order formula, so the conjecture is consistent with and follows from that theorem.
record.source_name: Zilin Jiang and Alexandr Polyanskii, “Forbidden subgraphs for graphs of bounded spectral radius, with applications to equiangular lines”, arXiv:1708.02317 (2019).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1606.06620](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.06620).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.02317

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2017). “This conjecture was later confirmed by Neumaier (see also ).”

record.title: The spectral-radius-order conjecture for equiangular lines
record.statement:
Let $N_\alpha(n)$ denote the maximum number of equiangular lines in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with angle $\arccos\alpha$. For $\alpha\in(0,1)$, define

$$
\lambda=\frac{1-\alpha}{2\alpha}
$$

and let $k(\lambda)$ be the smallest order of a graph with spectral radius $\lambda$, setting $k(\lambda)=\infty$ if no graph has spectral radius $\lambda$. **Spectral-radius-order conjecture.**

$$
N_\alpha(n)=\frac{k(\lambda)}{k(\lambda)-1}\,n+O(1).
$$

If $k(\lambda)=\infty$, this means $N_\alpha(n)=n+O(1)$. The conjecture is presented as a stronger form of the odd-reciprocal conjecture, while the paper proves it when $\lambda\le\sqrt{2+\sqrt{5}}$ and gives an exact bound in one further algebraic-integer case; it remains open in general.
record.source_name: Zilin Jiang and Alexandr Polyanskii, “Forbidden subgraphs for graphs of bounded spectral radius, with applications to equiangular lines”, arXiv:1708.02317 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.02317

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2017). “This conjecture was later confirmed by Neumaier (see also ).”

record.title: Multiplicity conjecture for the second-largest eigenvalue
record.statement:
For $\lambda>0$, let $k(\lambda)$ be the smallest order of a graph with spectral radius $\lambda$, or $\infty$ if no such graph exists, and let $v(G)$ denote the order of a graph $G$. **Multiplicity conjecture.** There exist graphs $G_1,\dots,G_n$, each of spectral radius greater than $\lambda$, such that every connected graph $G$ avoiding all of them as subgraphs satisfies: if $\lambda$ is the second-largest eigenvalue of $G$, then its multiplicity is at most

$$
\frac{v(G)}{k(\lambda)}.
$$

The authors state that their proof strategy would resolve the spectral-radius-order conjecture provided this forbidden-subgraph and eigenvalue-multiplicity connection holds; no proof or disproof is supplied here.
record.source_name: Zilin Jiang and Alexandr Polyanskii, “Forbidden subgraphs for graphs of bounded spectral radius, with applications to equiangular lines”, arXiv:1708.02317 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.02317

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2017). “This conjecture was later confirmed by Neumaier (see also ).”

record.title: Lehmann's conjecture on the Iitaka dimension of contracted cycles
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a projective variety of dimension $n$, let $\pi:X\to Z$ be a surjective morphism of projective varieties of relative dimension $e$, and let $\alpha\in\operatorname{\overline{Eff}}_k(X)_{\mathbb{Z}}$ have $\pi$-contractibility index $c$, meaning that $c$ is the largest non-negative integer at most $k$ such that $\alpha\cdot\pi^*A^{k-c+1}=0$ for an ample divisor $A$ on $Z$. **Lehmann's conjecture.** If

$$
k-\dim Z<c<e,
$$

then

$$
\kappa(\alpha)\leq n-c.
$$

The surrounding statement records the other expected bounds as theorems, while this intermediate-contractibility case is presented as the conjectural part. It concerns how the Iitaka dimension is constrained when a cycle is contracted by a morphism without falling into the two extremal cases.
record.source_name: Brian Lehmann, “Iitaka dimension for cycles”, arXiv:1708.02957 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.02957

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

record.title: Čada–Kaneko–Ryjáček conjecture on minimum color degree and rainbow cycles
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an edge-colored graph with $n=|V(G)|$ vertices, and let $\delta^c(G)$ denote its minimum color degree. For an integer $k$, a **rainbow cycle** is a cycle whose edges have pairwise distinct colors.

**Čada–Kaneko–Ryjáček conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^c(G)\geq \frac{n+k}{2},
$$

then $G$ contains a rainbow-cycle subgraph of length at least $k$.

This conjecture generalizes the known sufficient condition that $\delta^c(G)>\frac{n}{2}+2$ guarantees a rainbow cycle of length at least four. The source does not provide evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Wipawee Tangjai, “The minimum color degree and a large rainbow cycle in an edge-colored graph”, arXiv:1708.04187 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.04187

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

record.title: Blue-red decomposition conjecture for 3-connected cubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $3$-connected, cubic graph. A **blue-red decomposition** of $G$ is a coloring of its vertices blue and red; the blue subgraph and red subgraph are the subgraphs induced by the vertices of the respective colors, and a $4$-path is a path with four vertices.

**Blue-red decomposition conjecture.** The vertices of $G$ can be colored blue and red such that the blue subgraph has maximum degree $1$ (that is, it consists of a matching and some isolated vertices), while the red subgraph has minimum degree at least $1$ and contains no $4$-path.

This decomposition is used in the paper's approach to Wegner's conjecture on coloring squares of planar graphs. The supplied material gives no evidence that the blue-red decomposition conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Carsten Thomassen, “The square of a planar cubic graph is 7-colorable”, arXiv:1708.04406 (2017).

record.title: The duality between geometric thickness and geometric antithickness
record.statement: For a graph, geometric thickness is the minimum number of plane geometric layers in a straight-line drawing, and geometric antithickness is the minimum number of geometric thrackles whose edge sets partition the graph. **Geometric duality conjecture.** Geometric thickness and geometric antithickness are tied. The paper presents this as one of the proposed positive dualities between thickness-type parameters; its resolution is not given here.
record.source_name: Vida Dujmović and David R. Wood, “Thickness and Antithickness of Graphs”, arXiv:1708.04773 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.04773

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2017). “Thus a seemingly easier open problem is to decide whether planar graphs have bounded geometric antithickness.”

record.title: The duality between book thickness and convex antithickness
record.statement: For a graph, book thickness is the minimum number of pages in a book embedding, and convex antithickness is the minimum number of convex geometric thrackles in a straight-line drawing. **Book–convex-antithickness duality conjecture.** Book thickness and convex antithickness are tied. This is stated alongside the proposed geometric thickness–geometric antithickness duality; no resolution is supplied in the paper excerpt.

record.title: Dankelmann–Oellermann–Swart conjecture on average Steiner distance
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n\geq k$, and let $\mu(G)$ denote its average distance and $\mu_k(G)$ its average Steiner $k$-distance. **Dankelmann–Oellermann–Swart conjecture.** For $3\leq k\leq n$,

$$
\mu_k(G)\geq 3\frac{k-1}{k+1}\mu(G).
$$

Equivalently, the smallest ratio $\mu_k(G)/\mu(G)$ is conjectured to be attained by the path. The source describes the corresponding lower-bound problem as open.
record.source_name: Yaping Mao, “Steiner Distance in Graphs–A Survey”, arXiv:1708.05779 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.05779

record.title: Andrews et al.'s twin chromatic index conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order at least $3$ that is not a $5$-cycle. A twin edge coloring is a proper edge labeling by elements of $\mathbb{Z}_k$ whose induced vertex sums properly color $G$; the least such $k$ is the twin chromatic index, denoted by $\chi'_t(G)$, and $\Delta(G)$ is the maximum degree.

**Andrews et al.'s conjecture.** If $G$ is a connected graph of order at least $3$ that is not a $5$-cycle, then

$$
\chi'_t(G)\leq \Delta(G)+2.
$$

The conjecture was stated by Andrews et al. and verified there for some classes of graphs. No resolution is given in the supplied text, so the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Sylwia Cichacz and Jakub Przybyło, “Group twin coloring of graphs”, arXiv:1708.05902 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.05902

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

record.title: Minimum semidefinite rank conjecture for graphs of large girth
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n\geq 2$ vertices, and let $k\geq 4$ be an integer. The **minimum semidefinite rank** ${\rm msr}(G)$ is the smallest rank among all positive semidefinite Hermitian matrices with graph $G$. The **girth** of $G$ is the length of its shortest cycle.

**Large-girth minimum semidefinite rank conjecture.** If $G$ has girth at least $k$, then

$$
{\rm msr}(G)\geq \left(\frac{k-2}{k}\right)n.
$$

This conjecture seeks to generalize the known lower bound ${\rm msr}(G)\geq n/2$ for connected triangle-free graphs, viewing triangle-freeness as a girth lower bound. Its status is not determined by the supplied source information.
record.source_name: Louis Deaett and H. Tracy Hall, “Orthogonal representations of Steiner triple system incidence graphs”, arXiv:1708.07741 (2017).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1606.00697](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.00697).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.07741

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

record.title: Conjecture on disjoint properly colored cycles in edge-colored complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an edge-colored complete graph on $n$ vertices. Write $cDelta^{mon}(G)$ for its maximum monochromatic degree, and call a cycle **properly colored** if consecutive edges have different colors. **Disjoint properly colored cycle conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta^{mon}(G)\leq n-3k+1,
$$

then $G$ contains $k$ vertex-disjoint properly colored cycles, each of length at most $4$.

This would improve the sufficient bound $\Delta^{mon}(G)\leq n-4k+2$ obtained by repeatedly deleting short properly colored cycles, and would give the best possible function sought in the surrounding discussion. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ruonan Li, Hajo Broersma and Shenggui Zhang, “Vertex-disjoint properly edge-colored cycles in edge-colored complete graphs”, arXiv:1708.08641 (2017).

record.title: Hernandez–Sethuraman theta-quotient conjecture
record.statement:
Let $a,b\in\mathbb R_+$, and define the Jacobi theta function

$$
\vartheta_3(y)=\Theta_{\mathbb Z}(y)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}e^{-\pi n^2y}=1+2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}e^{-\pi n^2y},
$$

for $y\in\mathbb R_+$. **Hernandez–Sethuraman conjecture.** The function

$$
\frac{\vartheta_3(y)\,\vartheta_3(aby)}{\vartheta_3(ay)\,\vartheta_3(by)}
$$

attains its unique maximum at $1/\sqrt{ab}$. The paper later explains that the conjecture fails when $a<1<b$, where the indicated point is instead a minimum; thus the conjecture is refuted.
record.source_name: Esa V. Vesalainen and Anne-Maria Ernvall-Hytönen, “On the secrecy gain of -modular lattices”, arXiv:1708.09239 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.09239

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of August 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Rational-temperature walk-regularity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $n_G$ be its number of vertices, and let $S^V(G,\beta)$ denote its walk entropy at temperature $\beta\geq0$. The graph $G$ is **walk-regular** when every vertex is contained in the same number of closed walks of every length. **Rational-temperature conjecture.** A graph $G$ is walk-regular if and only if there exists a rational $\beta>0$ such that

$$
S^V(G,\beta)=\log n_G.
$$

The preceding result shows that a non-walk-regular graph can attain maximum walk entropy at only finitely many positive temperatures, while the source offers this rational-temperature strengthening as a further conjecture.
record.source_name: Kyle Kloster, Daniel Král' and Blair D. Sullivan, “Walk entropy and walk-regularity”, arXiv:1708.09700 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.09700

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

record.title: The disjoint domination number with a perfect matching is bounded by independence number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph containing a swap set. Let $DD_{\operatorname{m}}(G)$ denote the minimum size of a disjoint dominating set whose two parts are joined by a perfect matching, and let $\alpha(G)$ be the independence number of $G$. **Disjoint-domination independence conjecture.**

$$
DD_{\operatorname{m}}(G)\leq\alpha(G).
$$

The conjecture asserts the existence of a desired matching between two disjoint dominating sets whose total size is controlled by the independence number. The supplied text does not state whether this conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: William F. Klostermeyer, Margaret-Ellen Messinger and Alejandro Angeli Ayello, “Disjoint Dominating Sets with a Perfect Matching”, arXiv:1708.09774 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.09774

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2017). “An open question of was: is it true that $DD_{\textrm{m}}(P_3 \by P_n) = \gamma(P_3 \by P_n)+2$ when $n \equiv 1$ (mod $4$) for $n > 9$?”

record.title: The minimum conflict-free connection number conjecture for trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree of order $n$, and let $cfc(T)$ denote its conflict-free connection number, the smallest number of edge colors needed so that every two vertices are joined by a path containing a uniquely occurring color. **The minimum conflict-free connection number conjecture for trees.**

$$
cfc(T)\geq \lceil \log_2 n\rceil.
$$

Since $cfc(P_n)=\lceil \log_2 n\rceil$ is known, this conjecture says that the path has the least conflict-free connection number among all trees of order $n$.
record.source_name: Zhenzhen Li and Baoyindureng Wu, “On the maximum value of conflict-free verex-connection number of graphs”, arXiv:1709.01225 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.01225

record.title: The maximum-degree conjecture for rainbow matchings in bipartite multigraphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a bipartite multigraph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)$, and allow its edges to be coloured not necessarily properly. A **full rainbow matching** is a matching containing one edge of every colour. **The maximum-degree conjecture.** If every colour appears on at least $\Delta(G)+1$ edges, then $G$ has a full rainbow matching. This conjecture concerns rainbow matchings under bounded degree without proper edge-colouring. The paper states that related conjectures of this type are refuted later, but the supplied status evidence does not specifically resolve this candidate.
record.source_name: Pu Gao, Reshma Ramadurai, Ian Wanless and Nick Wormald, “Full rainbow matchings in graphs and hypergraphs”, arXiv:1709.02665 (2018).

record.title: The Section Property for Calabi--Yau and Fano Fermat hypersurfaces
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a Fermat hypersurface of degree $d$ and dimension parameter $r$, in the notation of the paper. Let $(\star)$ denote the distinguished-marking condition defined there. **Fermat hypersurface conjecture.** If

$$
d\leq r+2,
$$

so that the Fermat hypersurface is Calabi--Yau or Fano, then $X$ satisfies Condition $(\star)$. The paper states that it cannot determine whether other Fermat hypersurfaces satisfy this condition; the conjecture therefore isolates the Calabi--Yau and Fano range.

record.title: Baryshnikov–Ghrist monotonicity conjecture for unimodal p-category
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space and let $f:X\to[0,\infty)$ be a continuous function. For $p\in(0,\infty]$, let $\operatorname{{\bf ucat}}^p(f)$ denote the minimum number of unimodal functions needed to represent $f$ by an $\ell^p$-combination, with $p=\infty$ interpreted as pointwise maxima. **Baryshnikov–Ghrist monotonicity conjecture.** If $0<p_1<p_2\leq\infty$, then

$$
\operatorname{{\bf ucat}}^{p_1}(f)\leq\operatorname{{\bf ucat}}^{p_2}(f).
$$

Equivalently, the unimodal $p$-category is monotone nondecreasing in $p$. The conjecture is motivated by the role of unimodal category in obtaining bounds in higher dimensions; this paper proves it for functions on $\mathbb R$ and $S^1$, but gives counterexamples on certain graphs and on the Euclidean plane, so the general statement is refuted.
record.source_name: Dejan Govc, “Unimodal Category and the Monotonicity Conjecture”, arXiv:1709.06547 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.06547

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The chart simplification conjecture for branched covering surface-knots
record.statement:
Let $(F,\Gamma)$ be a branched covering surface-knot of degree $N$. The quantities $u(F,\Gamma)$ and $u_w(F,\Gamma)$ denote, respectively, the maximum and weak maximum numbers of 1-handles required in the relevant chart simplification processes.

**Chart simplification conjecture.**

$$
u(F,\Gamma) \leq \max\{u_w(F,\Gamma),N-1\}.
$$

This conjecture predicts that the simplification number is controlled by the weak simplification number and the degree. It is presented here as a conjecture previously given in the cited work; no resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Inasa Nakamura, “Simplifying branched covering surface-knots by chart moves involving black vertices”, arXiv:1709.07762 (2018).

record.title: Van Dam–Sotirov's smallest-eigenvalue conjecture for Hamming graphs
record.statement:
Let $q \ge 2$ and $d \ge 1$ be integers, let $Q$ be a set of size $q$, and let $H(d,q,j)$ be the distance-$j$ graph of the Hamming scheme on $Q^d$, whose eigenvalues are $K_j(i)$, where

$$
K_j(i)=\sum_{h=0}^j(-1)^h(q-1)^{j-h}\binom{i}{h}\binom{d-i}{j-h}.
$$

**Van Dam–Sotirov's conjecture.** If $j\ge d-\frac{d-1}{q}$, with $j$ even when $q=2$, then the smallest eigenvalue of $H(d,q,j)$ is $K_j(1)$. The conjecture was proved in the paper: the binary case was already known, and the nonbinary case is settled here, so it is solved.
record.source_name: Andries E. Brouwer, Sebastian M. Cioabă, Ferdinand Ihringer and Matt McGinnis, “The smallest eigenvalues of Hamming graphs, Johnson graphs and other distance-regular graphs with classical parameters”, arXiv:1709.09011 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.09011

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Karloff's smallest-eigenvalue conjecture for distance graphs of Johnson graphs
record.statement:
Let $J(n,d,j)$ be the distance-$j$ graph of the Johnson graph on the $d$-subsets of an $n$-set, and let its eigenvalues be $E_j(i)$, where

$$
E_j(i)=\sum_{h=0}^i(-1)^{i-h}\binom{i}{h}\binom{d-h}{j}\binom{n-d-i+h}{n-d-j}.
$$

**Karloff's conjecture.** If $n=2d$ and $j>d/2$, then the smallest eigenvalue of $J(n,d,j)$ is $E_j(1)$. The surrounding text says that this conjecture is settled in the paper, so the claim is solved.
record.source_name: Andries E. Brouwer, Sebastian M. Cioabă, Ferdinand Ihringer and Matt McGinnis, “The smallest eigenvalues of Hamming graphs, Johnson graphs and other distance-regular graphs with classical parameters”, arXiv:1709.09011 (2018).

record.title: Unimodality conjecture for dual polar scheme eigenvalues
record.statement:
Let $C_q(d,e)$ be the dual polar association scheme with diameter $d$, and let $C_j(i)$ denote the eigenvalue in row $i$ and column $j$, for $0\le i,j\le d$. For fixed $j$, consider the sequence $|C_j(i)|$.

**Unimodality conjecture for dual polar schemes.** The sequence $|C_j(i)|$ is unimodal except when $(q,e)=(2,1)$ or $(q,e,j)=(2,2,d-4)$ with $8\le d\le12$. If its minimum is at $i_0$, and $i_1=\lfloor(d+e+1)/2\rfloor$, then $i_0=i_1$ for $e=0,\frac12,\frac32$, and $|i_0-i_1|\le1$ for $e=1,2$, except that $i_0=i_1-2$ for $(q,e,j,d)=(2,1,3,4),(2,2,3,7)$. The source presents this as a conjecture and gives no resolution, so it remains open.

record.title: The combinatorial rigidity conjecture for unicritical and exponential families
record.statement: Let ${\cal F}$ be the exponential family or a family of unicritical polynomials. For $f\in{\cal F}$, its orbit portrait is the collection of all tuples of rays landing at parabolic and repelling points; two maps have the same combinatorics when their orbit portraits agree. **Combinatorial rigidity conjecture.** If $f_c,f_{c'}\in{\cal F}$ have all periodic points repelling, then they have the same orbit portrait if and only if $c=c'$. The conjecture asserts that repelling-cycle combinatorics determine the parameter in these families. The survey presents it as open, while noting that the analogous statement is false for non-unicritical cubic polynomials.

record.title: Collins–Trenk conjecture on the distinguishing chromatic number of graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with girth at least $5$, let $Delta$ denote its maximum degree, and let $chi_D(G)$ denote its distinguishing chromatic number. **Collins–Trenk conjecture.** If $Delta
e 3$ or greater, then

$$
chi_D(G) \leq Delta+1.
$$

This conjecture asks for a uniform upper bound on the distinguishing chromatic number in terms of the maximum degree for connected graphs of girth at least five. The supplied text does not indicate whether it has been resolved.

record.title: The Clifford torus energy minimization conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a Lagrangian torus in $\mathbb{C}P^2$, with energy functional

$$
E(\Sigma)=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Sigma}V\,dx\wedge dy=A(\Sigma)+\frac{1}{8}W(\Sigma),
$$

where $A(\Sigma)$ is its area and $W(\Sigma)$ is the integral of the squared norm of its mean curvature vector. Let $\Sigma_{Cl}$ be the Clifford torus, whose energy is

$$
E(\Sigma_{Cl})=\frac{4\pi^2}{3\sqrt{3}}.
$$

**Clifford torus energy minimization conjecture.** The minimum of the energy functional is attained on the Clifford torus.

This conjecture proposes that the Clifford torus minimizes the geometric energy among Lagrangian tori in $\mathbb{C}P^2$; the supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved.

record.title: The flow category moves conjecture
record.statement:
A **framed flow category** is a flow category equipped with framing data, and its associated stable homotopy type is the stable homotopy invariant constructed from that framing. Two framed flow categories are **move equivalent** if they are related by a finite sequence of flow category moves: perturbation, stabilization, handle cancellation, and the extended Whitney trick.

**Flow category moves conjecture.** If two framed flow categories determine the same stable homotopy type, then they are move equivalent.

These moves preserve the associated stable homotopy type and model operations familiar from Morse theory. The conjecture asserts that they provide a complete calculus for framed flow categories, but the supplied source does not state a resolution.

record.title: Calabi–Yau property conjecture for the moduli stack of one-dimensional sheaves
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective Calabi–Yau threefold, let $\beta\in N_1(X)$, and let $\mathcal{M}_X(\beta)$ be the moduli stack of one-dimensional sheaves with class $\beta$. Let $\operatorname{Chow}_X(\beta)$ be the Chow variety and let the Hilbert–Chow map send a sheaf to its fundamental one-cycle. The stack $\mathcal{M}_X(\beta)$ is Calabi–Yau at every point $\gamma\in\operatorname{Chow}_X(\beta)$ for the Hilbert–Chow map.

This conjectural Calabi–Yau condition is used to construct the relevant perverse sheaves and invariants. The paper proves the condition for the local Calabi–Yau threefold $X=\operatorname{Tot}_S(K_S)$ when $S$ is a smooth projective surface, but the general projective Calabi–Yau case remains open.

record.title: Mader's nonseparating dipath conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ and $m$ be positive integers, and let $D$ be a $k$-connected digraph. Denote its minimum outdegree and indegree by $\delta^+(D)$ and $\delta^-(D)$, and define its minimum semi-degree by

$$
\delta(D)=\min\{\delta^+(D),\delta^-(D)\}.
$$

A dipath $P$ has order $m$ when it contains $m$ vertices, and $\kappa(D)$ denotes vertex-connectivity.

**Mader's nonseparating dipath conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(D)\geq 2k+m-1,
$$

then $D$ has a dipath $P$ of order $m$ such that

$$
\kappa(D-V(P))\geq k.
$$

This is the digraph analogue of the nonseparating path conjecture. At the time of the paper, it had been verified only for $m=1$, and for $m=2$ with $k=1$; the general assertion remains open.

record.title: Grigoriev–Koshevoy's exponential lower-bound conjecture for skew-Schur polynomials
record.statement:
Let $s_{\lambda/\mu}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ be the skew-Schur polynomial, where $\lambda/\mu$ is a skew shape, and let $\operatorname{Trop}(s_{\lambda/\mu})$ denote its tropicalization. The **tropical semiring complexity** of a tropical polynomial is the smallest number of gates in an arithmetic circuit over $({\mathbb R},\oplus,\odot)$ that computes it using the tropical semiring axioms.

**Grigoriev–Koshevoy's conjecture.** The tropical semiring complexity of $\operatorname{Trop}(s_{\lambda/\mu})$ is at least exponential.

This concerns the circuit complexity of tropicalizations of skew-Schur polynomials. The supplied source attributes the statement to Section 5 of Grigoriev and Koshevoy, but gives no resolution evidence; its status is therefore open.

record.title: Linear growth conjecture for Berge saturation numbers
record.statement:
Let $k$ be fixed, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be any fixed finite family of graphs. Write $\operatorname{sat}_k(n,\text{Berge-}\mathcal{F})$ for the minimum number of edges in a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices that is Berge-$\mathcal{F}$-saturated. **Linear growth conjecture for Berge saturation numbers.** For any fixed finite family of graphs $\mathcal{F}$,

$$
\operatorname{sat}_k(n,\text{Berge-}\mathcal{F})=O(n).
$$

Classical graph saturation numbers are known to be linear in $n$, whereas general $k$-uniform hypergraph saturation has the upper bound $O(n^{k-1})$. The conjecture proposes linear growth for the Berge-saturation setting, but the paper does not establish it in general.

record.title: Cohen–Lenstra conjecture for the largest torsion group in random complexes
record.statement:
Let $LT(n)$ be the largest torsion group found in the first homology during the torsion burst of the Linial–Meshulam process. For a fixed prime $q$, let the Sylow $q$-subgroup of $LT(n)$ be the maximal subgroup of order a power of $q$. **Cohen–Lenstra conjecture for $LT(n)$.** For a fixed prime $q$, the Sylow $q$-subgroup of $LT(n)$ is asymptotically distributed according to the Cohen–Lenstra distribution, which assigns probability

$$
\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}(1-q^{-k})}{|\operatorname{Aut}(G)|}
$$

to any finite abelian $q$-group $G$. This is motivated by analogous models of random abelian groups and supported in the paper by computational experiments; the asserted limiting distribution remains conjectural.
record.source_name: Matthew Kahle, Frank Lutz, Andrew Newman and Kyle Parsons, “Cohen–Lenstra heuristics for torsion in homology of random complexes”, arXiv:1710.05683 (2018).

record.title: The critical-time conjecture for stationary interfaces of the parabolic p-Laplace equation
record.statement:
Let $u$ solve the one-dimensional $p$-parabolic boundary-value problem

$$
u_t-
Delta_p u=0
$$

on $(-1,1)\times(0,T)$ with boundary values $u(-1,t)=0$, $u(1,t)=1$, and initial value $u(x,0)=x_+^{\frac{p}{p-2}}$. For the restriction to $(0,1)\times(0,T)$, let $c_p$ and $c_0$ be the constants from the preceding finite-speed-of-propagation estimate, and set $\hat t=(c_p c_0)^{p-2}$. **Critical-time conjecture.** The critical time $\hat t=(c_p c_0)^{p-2}$ is the largest time such that $u(0,t)=0$. This concerns whether the interface remains stationary exactly up to the time supplied by the estimate; the provided passage does not state whether the claim has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Multicolor Ramsey conjecture for disjoint unions of three-vertex paths
record.statement:
Let $P_3$ be the path on three vertices, and let $gr_k(K_3:n_1P_3,\ldots,n_kP_3)$ denote the corresponding Gallai-Ramsey number. For positive integers $k,n_1,n_2,\ldots,n_k$ with $n_1=\max\{n_i\}$, **the multicolor $P_3$ Ramsey conjecture.**

$$
R(n_1P_3,n_2P_3,\ldots,n_kP_3)=gr_k(K_3:n_1P_3,n_2P_3,\ldots,n_kP_3)=2n_1+1+\sum_{i=1}^k(n_i-1).
$$

The claim would determine the general multicolor classical Ramsey number for these linear forests and identify it with the Gallai-Ramsey number; the source says that this classical number is not known in general.

record.title: Finite Dolnikov–Eckhoff conjecture for elliptical disks
record.statement:
Let $B=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2\leq1\}$ be the unit disk. Let $E\subset\mathbb R^2$ be an elliptical disk, let $Z\subset\partial E$ satisfy $\#Z\leq5$, and suppose that $E$ has minimum area among all elliptic disks containing $Z$. Define

$$
R=R(Z)=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\{x\}\cup Z\text{ satisfies }T(B,3)\}.
$$

**Finite Dolnikov–Eckhoff conjecture.** The set $R\cap E$ satisfies

$$
T\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}B\right).
$$

This conjecture is presented as apparently stronger than the Dolnikov–Eckhoff conjecture and is part of the paper’s proposed finite reduction. Its resolution is not established in the supplied text.
